findings.title: Async decoration writes have no durability or ordering contract
findings.location: §3.2 Latency Budget; §2 SDR-07-006; §8.2 Decoration Payload Shape; §12 ACC-21/ACC-22
findings.evidence: "Decoration write (async) | — | — | Fire-and-forget; not in critical path"; "Every resolution records its citation in a decoration payload"; ACC-21/22 require "DHF records ... citation".
findings.problem: The spec requires DHF citation recording but makes the write fire-and-forget with no retry, idempotency, or sequencing definition relative to the tool-call/entry lifecycle.
findings.why_it_matters: The audit trail can be silently lost or written out of order while the tool call still executes, which breaks a core requirement and is hard to detect or recover from.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a durable write path: either await the decoration write before reporting success, or use an outbox/queue with retries, idempotency keys, and an explicit failure state that prevents claiming the resolution was recorded when it was not.

findings.title: Resolution cardinality is internally inconsistent for multi-domain utterances
findings.location: §3.1 Four-Stage Flow; §5.1 Role; §6.2 System Prompt; §6.4 Output Contract
findings.evidence: Stage 4 shows "resolved_terms: [ResolvedTerm, ...]" and "citations: [Citation, ...]"; §5.1 says one utterance may hit "threads, manufacturing, and materials domains simultaneously"; §6.2 says "select the ONE row"; §6.4 defines only a single `ResolvedTerm` result type.
findings.problem: The spec alternates between a multi-term pipeline result and a single-row resolution model without defining which contract is authoritative.
findings.why_it_matters: Implementation cannot know whether one call resolves one term or several, so planner/synthesis/tool-call integration and decoration payload shape will churn.
findings.proposed_fix: Choose one model and make all sections match: either restrict the service to one resolved term per call, or define an explicit multi-term result schema with per-term confidence, citation, and ambiguity behavior.

findings.title: IVocabRepository cannot enforce the required single repeatable-read snapshot per utterance
findings.evidence: "Policy: all queries within single read transaction; repeatable read isolation"; `IVocabRepository` exposes only independent per-method calls and no batch/session/transaction API.
findings.problem: The pipeline has no specified interface for executing multiple planner queries on one connection inside one repeatable-read transaction.
findings.why_it_matters: The stated consistency guarantee is not implementable without leaking transaction management out of the repository or changing the interface later.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a repository batch/read-session contract, e.g. `ExecuteAsync(IReadOnlyList<VocabQuery>)` or an explicit read-only unit-of-work that owns the transaction scope.

findings.title: Manufacturing is in scope but has no grammar, schema, or repository contract
findings.evidence: Scope and bouncer domains include `manufacturing`; §5.1 example says one utterance hits "threads, manufacturing, and materials"; there is no manufacturing grammar section and no `ManufacturingRow` or manufacturing repository method in §9.1.
findings.problem: A declared domain can be emitted by the bouncer/planner but cannot be resolved by any specified downstream contract.
findings.why_it_matters: This creates an implementation hole and test gap in a closed-set domain list the LLM is instructed to use.
findings.proposed_fix: Either remove `manufacturing` from the v1 closed domain set, or add its tables/DTOs, grammar rules, repository methods, synthesis behavior, and required tests.

findings.title: Material grammar depends on lookups that IVocabRepository does not expose
findings.evidence: "UNS <letter><5 digits>" maps to `vocab.materials.uns_number`; "ASTM ..." and "AMS ..." map to `vocab.canonical_terms.standard_source`; `IVocabRepository` only exposes `FindMaterialsByGradeNameAsync` and `GetMaterialAsync` for materials.
findings.problem: The documented UNS/ASTM/AMS planner paths cannot be implemented through the repository interface without adding raw SQL elsewhere or changing the contract.
findings.why_it_matters: This violates SDR-07-004 and guarantees downstream interface churn when material resolution is implemented.
findings.proposed_fix: Add explicit repository methods for UNS and standard-source lookups, or define a typed generic material lookup API that covers every selector documented in §5.3.

findings.title: Persisted decoration payload lacks an explicit JSON schema for polymorphic Resolution
findings.evidence: `public abstract record VocabularyResolution;` and `public required VocabularyResolution Resolution { get; init; }` are said to be serialized to the `payload` JSON column.
findings.problem: The stored payload depends on CLR polymorphic serialization details, but the spec does not define a stable discriminator, field set, or version for consumers.
findings.why_it_matters: SPEC-04 persistence and SPEC-06 rendering can break when serializer settings or subtypes change, and old rows may become unreadable.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify a concrete versioned JSON schema for each resolution variant with an explicit discriminator, and persist that schema instead of relying on default abstract-record serialization.

findings.title: Build-breaking latency tests depend on external LLM and network conditions
findings.evidence: "bouncer p95 latency under 600ms on test harness; fails the build if exceeded on CI" and "full pipeline p95 under 1.2s".
findings.problem: These tests require stable Anthropic/Railway/network timing that CI does not control.
findings.why_it_matters: The build will flap for environmental reasons unrelated to code changes, making the requirement unmaintainable.
findings.proposed_fix: Move latency verification to a dedicated performance environment with controlled baselines; keep CI on mocked or recorded timing contracts.

findings.title: Build-breaking semantic tests assume stable live-model outputs
findings.evidence: Tests require seeded utterances to match expected bouncer classifications/domains and synthesis outcomes, while both stages are defined as Sonnet 4.6 calls.
findings.problem: The spec does not define a frozen test double or captured-response harness, so model nondeterminism and vendor updates can break tests with no code change.
findings.why_it_matters: These requirements are not reproducibly verifiable in CI and will create constant false failures or pressure to weaken tests.
findings.proposed_fix: Define deterministic CI tests against mocked/captured model responses, and run live-model evaluations separately as non-blocking acceptance suites.

findings.title: Process-lifetime repository cache has no invalidation path for corpus hot-fixes
findings.evidence: "Entries are effectively immutable ... TTL is the process lifetime"; §9.2 says repeatable-read exists in case "a hot-fix migration runs".
findings.problem: The cache can continue serving stale canonical rows after a vocabulary hot-fix until the process restarts.
findings.why_it_matters: Returned parameters/citations can diverge from the database, and the spec's consistency story breaks during live corpus updates.
findings.proposed_fix: Add cache invalidation keyed to corpus/migration version, a database notification mechanism, or a bounded TTL shorter than expected hot-fix intervals.

findings.title: Security-event logging stores full rejected utterances without redaction
findings.evidence: "logged at LogLevel.Warning with the full utterance text"; candidate domains include `medical` in §4.2.
findings.problem: Rejected transcripts may contain PHI, proprietary design details, or attacker-supplied secrets, yet the spec routes full text into monitoring logs.
findings.why_it_matters: This creates unnecessary data-exposure and compliance risk in a system that explicitly touches medical vocabulary.
findings.proposed_fix: Redact or hash utterance text by default, or route full text only to a restricted security log sink with explicit retention and access controls.

top_3_must_fix: Replace fire-and-forget decoration writes with a durable, ordered, idempotent DHF write contract.
Resolve the single-term vs multi-term contradiction in the VocabularyResolution contract before implementation starts.
Add a repository batch/read-session API that actually supports one repeatable-read snapshot for all queries in an utterance.
